$comment: Generated from Go TOML types and the Cobra command registry. Run go generate ./internal/cli; do not edit manually.
description: Editor assistance for WTF configuration. Runtime validation remains authoritative; schema default annotations do not apply inherited settings.

here.description: Inspect the current managed workspace CLI: --here. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

json.description: Emit one versioned JSON result; never prompt CLI: --json / -j. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

doctor.description: Check JJ installation and user identity, GitHub authentication, and the repository's Codex Linear MCP connection and workspace identity. Inspect retained workspace stages, claims and failures. Checks are bounded; remote authentication may contact GitHub and Linear. Does not install tools, start project services or run project hooks. Missing JJ prerequisites or unhealthy workspace state return a nonzero exit status; optional GitHub/Linear warnings do not. Example: wtf doctor --here --json.

hook list.description: Load the hook module and list names. No hook function is invoked. Module declarations should be side-effect free. Example: wtf hook list --json.

hook run.description: Invoke an explicitly registered project hook under its workspace lock. Arguments after -- reach request.args unchanged. Records stages and stops on failure. Example: wtf hook run test -- --verbose.

init.description: Register the current JJ repository and workspace, then run its configured init override. new uses this same registration and preparation lifecycle after creating a workspace. Repeated init preserves identity and lets reusable stages verify completed work. JSON registration codes are initialized or already_initialized; hook failures remain errors with retained stage records. Project arguments must follow --. Example: wtf init --json -- --compose.

all.description: Include removed workspace records; active workspaces are shown by default CLI: --all / -a. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

checks.description: Show GitHub CI check counts for the published PR head CLI: --checks / -c. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

global.description: List all registered repositories CLI: --global. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

here.description: Only the current managed workspace CLI: --here. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

hook.description: Show local hook stages (successful/recorded), not GitHub CI CLI: --hook / -k. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

json.description: Emit one versioned JSON result; never prompt CLI: --json / -j. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

pr.description: Show PRs with Linear-first review links and GitHub fallback CLI: --pr / -p. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

refresh.description: Request live PR metadata (already automatic with --pr) CLI: --refresh. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

select.description: Return only the selected path; render the picker on stderr for shell navigation CLI: --select. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

list.description:
Browse active workspaces with arrow keys; Enter selects, Esc cancels. The view paginates to your terminal size. list, ls, switch, sw and w are the same command. An optional NAME resolves a workspace directly.

Inside a repository, show its workspaces; from a parent directory, show repositories beneath it. --global includes all registered repositories, --all includes removed records.

--hook adds local stages, not CI. --pr adds GitHub PR status; each invocation performs a bounded live lookup. JSON and redirected output never prompt. With shell integration, selection changes your directory.

Examples:
  wtf list
  wtf sw -p
  wtf ls --all --json

from.description: JJ parent revision for the new workspace CLI: --from / -f. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

new.description: Create an owned sibling JJ workspace. --from defaults to trunk(). The explicitly registered Lua override can check/block creation and delegate once to the default. Arguments after -- reach request.args unchanged; project scripts interpret them. Stages run serially; failures retain completed work. Example: wtf new agent-a -f @ -- --compose.

ports claim.description: Atomically claim a port against other workspaces in this JJ repository. Project hooks choose availability/retry policy. Cross-repository leases are deferred. Example: wtf ports claim frontend --port 3000 --json.

ports list.description: Read claims, without checking listeners or choosing ports. Registry claims are not socket reservations. Example: wtf ports list --json.

ports release.description: Release only the current workspace's named claim. Does not stop a service. Example: wtf ports release frontend --json.

remove.description: Invoke the target workspace's remove override before native removal. Refuses current/adopted workspaces, identity mismatch, remaining external claims and changed source files. Failures retain cleanup state. Example: wtf remove agent-a --json.

json.description: Emit one versioned JSON result; never prompt CLI: --json / -j. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

run.description: Run an argv-based TOML task in the current managed workspace, recording its result. Arguments after -- are forwarded literally. Tasks do not reuse results by default. Example: wtf run test -- tests/auth.

json.description: Emit one versioned JSON result; never prompt CLI: --json / -j. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

validate.description: Parse strict config and compile the Lua file without executing it. Does not run hooks, register workspaces or snapshot JJ state. Example: wtf validate --json.

json.description: Emit one versioned JSON result; never prompt CLI: --json / -j. Explicit CLI flags override inherited TOML defaults.

version.description: Show the local pilot version; does not update any installed binary. Example: wtf version --json.

commands.description: Defaults for registered command flags. Precedence is global, outer parent, nearest parent, leaf, then explicit CLI flags. These schema defaults are annotations and do not perform the merge.

lua.description: Explicit Lua registration module relative to .wtf, such as hooks/init.lua. Filenames never register hooks; the returned hooks/overrides table does. Project modules may be imported with require.

command.description: Command argv, executed directly without shell interpolation. Additional task arguments are appended literally.

inputs.description: Project-relative files or directories included in the recorded stage fingerprint. Runtime checks reject escaping paths.

timeout_seconds.description: Task timeout in seconds. Omitted or zero uses 120 seconds.

tasks.description: Named project tasks. Tasks use the selected project's configuration rather than inherited command defaults.
